independence: A reviewer other than the authoring model/run assigns every behavioral/quality result from actual output and evidence; the runner never self-grades. Variant mapping and source instructions are withheld; root names visible in responses may partially reveal identity.
authorityRule: Every required authority/preservation check must pass in all three matched repetitions. Unavailable required tools/artifacts are unverified, not a passing output; no partial scenario can certify rendered/image quality.

scores.1: Major task, readability or consistency failures
scores.2: Usable but notable hierarchy, state, or fidelity shortcomings
scores.3: Clear, coherent, usable and faithful across requested evidence/state coverage
scores.4: Strong, well-resolved work with accurate detail and no material requested-outcome defect

aggregateRule: Each applicable dimension >=3; candidate aggregate quality must not fall below matched baseline aggregate. No noise margin or expanded samples are authorized; conflicting/insufficient evidence stays inconclusive.
efficiencyRule: Compare observed total input/output and loaded instruction bytes (never call bytes tokens), actual image calls and evidence quality. Median token improvement requires comparable runtime token telemetry or a separately named verified tokenizer. Token totals include host overhead; no skill-only token claim. No latency/cost claim from tokens alone.
notAutomatic: Browser metrics are observations for independent review, not aesthetic grades.
A screenshot cannot prove keyboard behavior.
An image prompt is not an image.
A response-only pilot cannot certify rendered or generated-image quality.
